title: The breath the demons couldn't pierce
hookLine: the gods and the demons were at war, and the gods reached for a song. the Chandogya tells which breath could carry it
carry: prana: the breath evil couldn't pierce
tomorrow: do the sounds between the words matter?
last: FROM THE GROUND UP TO OM.

lines: THE GODS AND THE DEMONS AT WAR.
THE GODS REACH FOR A SONG.
cards: The gods and the demons were at war. That's how the story starts, in the second section of the Chandogya Upanishad. And the gods decide their weapon will be a song.
Not a spear, not a trick: the udgitha, the high chant. With this, they say, we'll overcome them.
But a chant needs something to carry it, so the gods try one part of a person after another, and the demons follow them to each. Today: which breath can hold the song.

teach.h: NOSE, SPEECH, EYE, EAR, MIND: PIERCED.
teach.b: In paraphrase, it goes like this. First the gods sing the chant as the breath in the nose.
The demons pierce it with evil, and that, the text says, is why we smell both the sweet and the foul. Next, speech. Pierced: that's why we speak both truth and falsehood.
Then the eye, and we see both what's fitting and what isn't. Then the ear, and we hear both. Then the mind, and we think both kinds of thoughts.

teach.h: THE MAIN BREATH: THE DEMONS SCATTER.
teach.b: Then the gods sing the chant as the breath in the mouth, the main breath, the one that keeps a body alive.

The demons rush at it and scatter, the text says, the way a lump of earth flung at a solid rock breaks into pieces. Here's the teaching folded inside. Every sense in us is mixed; the same tongue blesses and lies.
But underneath them is prana, the life-breath, going in and out on good days and bad, and in this story it's the one thing evil couldn't break.
So the high chant is sung as prana: the song rides on the breath that keeps the singer alive.

teach.h: IN SANDHYA, THE BREATH COMES FIRST.
teach.b: Hindu practice still puts the breath first.
In sandhya, the daily prayers at dawn and dusk built around the Gayatri, a few rounds of pranayama, measured breathing, come before the mantra, and many formal pujas open the same way.

teach.h: PRANA: THE BREATH EVIL COULDN'T PIERCE.
teach.b: Many teachers read this story as one old reason why: before you pray with a voice that can go either way, you begin from the breath that can't.

how: The story of the gods, the demons and the breath is taught from the second section of the Chandogya Upanishad, part of the Sama Veda's tradition, where the high chant is meditated on as the main breath, prana.

games.q: what does “the sama veda as song” mean?
o: a chant carried by prana, the breath that keeps us alive
a war song the demons used against the gods
a chant carried by the mind, the clearest of the senses

games.q: the gods' tries — tap the pairs.
p: the demons scatter like earth on rock

s: in the story, the main breath goes both ways like the senses
every sense was pierced and goes both ways. the main breath held, and the demons scattered.
speech fails because it can tell both truth and falsehood
the demons pierce it, and so speech goes both ways.
the demons break against the main breath like a lump of earth on rock
that's the Chandogya's picture: they scatter.

games.q: you're one of the gods. nose, speech, eye, ear and mind have all been pierced. what do you sing the chant as now?
o: the main breath, the breath in the mouth
games.why: the main breath. the demons rush at it and scatter like a lump of earth flung at a rock. the song rides on the breath that keeps you alive.

practice: Notice a smell in the room, a sound, a thought passing, each with its own mood.
Then let them go and come to the breath: in slowly through the nose, a short easy pause, out slowly, the measured breath many Hindus take before sandhya or puja.
Keep it gentle and never strain; if anything feels uncomfortable, just breathe normally. A few rounds, then rest in the plain breath. If you pray, let that breath carry your prayer.

wordCard.voice: The Sama Veda as song. In the Chandogya, the high chant can't be carried by the senses or the mind. It's sung as the main breath, prana. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: breath, life-breath. In Chandogya 1.2 the high chant is sung as the main breath.

carryVoice: Your line: prana, the breath evil couldn't pierce. The song rides on it. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Chandogya Upanishad 1.2.1–8 (the gods and demons; the udgitha as nose-breath, speech, eye, ear, mind, then the main breath)
Sandhyavandana: pranayama before the Gayatri japa; pranayama at the opening of formal puja
